messages:
Sarah: raising this from support — customer reported p99 jump for model *gpt-small-v2* on dedicated pool eu-west-1 around 15:40 UTC. p95 also crept up. They see sporadic 700-900ms tails vs baseline ~120-150ms. attaching their ticket log and an example request payload. :warning:

Sarah: repro steps (from customer):
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Model: gpt-small-v2' -d '{"prompt":"summarize...","max_tokens":512}'
2) repeated at ~10 qps for 30s
3) observe occasional replies taking 800-900ms

Mike: thanks — can you paste the ticket id? also did they say this started after a deploy?

Sarah: ticket #CS-4239. Customer says it started ~10:00 UTC after a config change last night but not sure which. No deploy alerts in their logs.

Mike: ok looking at infra graphs now. Saw a step-up in continuous_batcher queue wait percentiles ~09:55-10:05 UTC. p99 hold-time spiked. Curious if timeout got increased.

Jordan: pulled runtime config for the pool; looks like someone toggled continuous_batcher hold_ms from 8 -> 40 for this pool at 09:50 UTC (change by ops user lena). That increases the maximum time a micro-request stays waiting to gather batch members. Useful for throughput, but raises tail latency.

Jordan: relevant config blob (redacted):
```
pool: eu-west-1-small
continuous_batcher: enabled
max_batch_size: 32
hold_ms: 40
min_batch_ms: 0
batch_timeout_policy: adaptive
```

Mike: that matches the p99 symptom — hold_ms at 40ms means some requests will wait up to that before firing; with additional scheduling and queue jitter, tails hit ~900ms. Runtime also does extra KV-cache lookups increasing variance.

Lena: I pushed that change to reduce drops and improve throughput for a big customer last night — I can rollback immediately. Sorry for the surprise. :grimacing:

Sarah: customer is breathing down support. can we mitigate first without full rollback? they prefer no restart.

Jordan: quick mitigations we can try (ordered by impact/complexity):
- reduce hold_ms to 6-8 (low risk, no restart)
- reduce max_batch_size to 16 for this pool (reduces queueing)
- enable per-model bypass: route requests for gpt-small-v2 to non-batched path (sync inference) — requires routing change but doable via weight adjustment
- temporarily enable strict latency SLO which disables batching for requests above Xms in the route (needs small rollout)

Mike: let's do smallest blast radius first. Jordan, can you set hold_ms=8 for pool eu-west-1-small as a config-only change? Then we can observe graphs and customer latency. If stable, follow up with max_batch_size=16. Call it a canary: 10% of pool? We can target via policy.

Jordan: doing it now — applying to 10% subset (shard 5).

ops-bot: config-change: applied continuous_batcher.hold_ms=8 to pool eu-west-1-small (shard 5) by Jordan at 2031004620.

Mike: watching grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/r1/batcher-metrics?orgId=1&var-pool=eu-west-1-small

Jordan: initial telemetry shows immediate p99 drop on shard 5 from ~850ms -> ~140ms. p95 dropped similarly. Good signal.

Lena: should I roll the change to 100%?

Mike: wait 10 more minutes. Also run quick load test to mimic customer's traffic: `hey loadtest --endpoint /v1/generate --qps 12 --duration 120 --model gpt-small-v2` — do from staging agent to avoid side effects.

Jordan: ran a 2-minute against a canary node. Logs show microbatch assembly wait reduced from ~28ms median -> ~6ms. snippet:
```
[2026-09-14T09:55:23Z] hold_wait_ms: 27.9 -> 6.1
[2026-09-14T09:55:23Z] batch_size_avg: 18 -> 9
[2026-09-14T09:55:23Z] service_latency_ms: 145 -> 135
```

Sarah: customer confirmed latency improved after we asked them to route 10% traffic to shard 5 temporarily — they see tails back to ~120-160ms. :tada:

Mike: great. Plan: 1) roll hold_ms=8 to 100% for that pool (non-disruptive config); 2) optionally set max_batch_size=20 to preserve some throughput; 3) add a tag on the pool and an alert rule for hold_ms>20 or p99>300ms to avoid surprise later; 4) doc the tradeoff in runbook.

Lena: rolling to 100% now.

deploy-bot: config-change: promoted continuous_batcher.hold_ms=8 to pool eu-west-1-small (100%) by Lena at 2031004665.

Jordan: after roll, aggregates look stable. We'll keep max_batch_size as-is for now; I'll open a follow-up to run throughput cost analysis if we drop max_batch_size.

Mike: filing incident summary and postmortem checklist. Items: trace config-change ownership, add pre-deploy checklist that flags hold_ms>10, add a smoke test that runs `p95/p99` against new batch configs in canary for 5 minutes.

Sarah: customer CS-4239 updated: latency regression resolved for now, they want a note before future batching config changes.

Mike: thanks everyone. I'll write the runbook section and add a dashboard panel showing hold_ms vs p99 with annotation for config changes.

Jordan: FYI: quick repro command for devs who want to reproduce locally (use a small model):
```
for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":64}' &
done; wait
```
This will surface microbatching hold effects at ~5-20 qps.

Lena: note for future: when applying throughput optimizations for a single tenant, prefer pool-level labels and clear rollback path.

Mike: marking this thread resolved for immediate action; will link postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:
